comparator.name: Global Sustainability Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 regulations govern the September 2026 entry. The 135 EC major comprises a 60 EC common core and 75 EC of track requirements and major choices. The illustrative Water, Climate & Ecosystems route follows official track order. The Philosophy of Science and Ethics course, ordinary Consultancy Project, Landscape Ecology and Nature Conservation, and Environmental Chemistry and Health illustrate the permitted non-track choices. The remaining 45 EC is the optional course profile, including at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. This curriculum example records the credit structure and academic progression. Individual course timeslots are confirmed at registration.

core: Integrated sustainability science linking natural and social systems
Climate, water, ecosystems, land and environmental degradation
Governance, policy, social change and environmental justice
Quantitative, qualitative, systems and field methods culminating in research
adjacent: Sustainable food systems, ecology and environmental health
Energy transitions, resources and circular material systems
questions: How can evidence-based solutions balance environmental and social systems?
How can governments, businesses and communities drive fair sustainability transitions?

alternatives.label: Water, Climate and Ecosystems
alternatives.concept: Study how climate, soils, aquifers and ecosystems interact. Use field sampling, geospatial analysis and statistics to investigate environmental change, and examine responses in delta management and sustainable farming.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how climate, soils, aquifers and ecosystems interact. Use field sampling, geospatial analysis and statistics to investigate environmental change, and examine responses in delta management and sustainable farming.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 8 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Sustainability Governance and Social Change
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions, law and communities shape sustainability transitions. Combine climate and environmental science with policy analysis, environmental justice, civil-society research and public communication.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how institutions, law and communities shape sustainability transitions. Combine climate and environmental science with policy analysis, environmental justice, civil-society research and public communication.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 8 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier prerequisites.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ecology, hazards, aquifers, sustainable farming and advanced quantitative depth with a sequenced law, politics, justice and communication curriculum.

alternatives.label: Sustainable Business, Energy and Resources
alternatives.concept: Study how firms and institutions respond to sustainability challenges. Link business models, market research and organisational change to renewable-energy design, resource use and circular material recovery.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how firms and institutions respond to sustainability challenges. Link business models, market research and organisational change to renewable-energy design, resource use and circular material recovery.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 10 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier prerequisites.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes entrepreneurship, circularity, renewable-system design, organisational innovation and international business for the closest route's ecology, hazards, water-management and advanced mathematics emphasis.

routeSelection.basis: The programme offers five formally parallel tracks. The common first year does not constitute a complete degree route. Water, Climate & Ecosystems comes first in Utrecht’s published study programme and is used as the example.

selection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Governance & Societal Transformation and a combined Business & Innovation plus Energy & Resources route. Both are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise course-difference floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Sustainability systems, climate, water and ecology
Both use interdisciplinary concepts to examine sustainability challenges. UCR introduces planetary boundaries and scientific tools through modelling and laboratory work.
Both study interactions among natural processes. UCR focuses on Earth systems, geology and field evidence.
Both examine climate processes, impacts and possible responses. Utrecht deepens the topic within the track.
Both examine biodiversity and ecological processes. Utrecht specialises in landscape ecology and conservation at advanced level.
Both examine water in soils and related natural systems. UCR focuses on soils and shallow aquifers, while Utrecht integrates water and ecosystem processes.
Utrecht surveys social-science approaches to sustainability. UCR develops related perspectives across economics, governance and environmental justice courses.
Both examine sustainability transitions, actors and possible interventions. Utrecht brings the perspectives together in a project. UCR focuses on governance and policy evaluation.
Both use chemistry to investigate environmental problems. UCR focuses on recovering materials and assessing remediation processes.
Both examine chemical processes and contaminants in environmental systems. Utrecht gives additional attention to human exposure and health.
Methods, projects, research and open space
Both develop mathematical tools for analysing systems. Utrecht embeds the tools in its sustainability programme.
Both develop research design and evidence skills. UCR adds statistical inference and quantitative analysis within this course.
Both develop statistical inference and hypothesis testing. UCR gives greater emphasis to mathematical foundations and simulation.
Both integrate evidence and disciplinary perspectives in an applied sustainability project. Utrecht uses fieldwork and stakeholder research on Texel. UCR investigates sustainability campaigns.
Utrecht requires a dedicated ecological field research course. UCR develops related field and laboratory skills in courses including Soils & Aquifers.
Utrecht offers philosophy of science and ethics as an intermediate major choice.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC individual thesis. UCR’s 15 EC optional independent research is shown separately from the scheduled courses.
Utrecht requires a separate consultancy project addressing an external organisation’s question.
Choose 45 EC, with at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. Options include extra major courses, a minor, study abroad or an internship. External courses require approval.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a 60 EC shared core with 75 EC of track requirements and major choices and a 45 EC optional course profile. Its separate ecological field research course, external consultancy project and individual thesis remain distinct features of this example.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Global Sustainability Science bachelor combines natural science, social science and research methods. Students begin with a shared foundation and then deepen their study through one of five tracks.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example follows Water, Climate & Ecosystems. The closest UCR option focuses on water, climate and ecology. The other two options explore sustainability through governance and social change, or through business, energy and resource use.
